comment: Single source of truth for all models supported by the Overmind platform. Each entry carries a 'backend' field (together | baseten). Models available on multiple backends appear as separate entries with their own inference/finetuning sub-configs. inference.gpu_type is the default for base-model inference (BF16 serving, single GPU). inference.lora_supported declares verified shared-base LoRA support for MoE models; dense models support it by default. inference.min_vram_gb is a measured minimum GPU capacity enforced for automatic inference selection, including short contexts. num_attn_layers/num_kv_heads/head_dim are used by gpu_selector.py to derive the optimal GPU + concurrency for a model at its serving max_model_len, including input and reserved output. For hybrid models (Qwen3.5), num_attn_layers counts only full-attention layers. Use model_registry.py helpers to filter by backend. To add/remove models, edit only this file. Baseten models train LoRA or Full on H100s/H200s via our TRL train.py; finetuning.context_length is the model's max trainable context = HF config max_position_embeddings (Qwen2.5 32768, Qwen3 dense 40960, Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8/Coder 262144, Llama 3.x / GPT-OSS / Antares-1B 131072, Antares-350M 32768, LFM2.5-230M/350M/1.2B 32768 per Liquid's documented window, LFM2.5-8B-A1B 128000, LFM2.5-2.6B 131072; train.py applies no RoPE scaling). context_length (top-level) is the published inference window (YaRN-extended where the vendor documents it: Qwen2.5≥7B and Qwen3 dense → 131072; Qwen2.5-0.5B stays 32768). Baseten itself imposes no per-model training context limit (max_seq_len up to 1048576, docs.baseten.co/engines/engine-builder-llm/engine-builder-config; training is arbitrary code, docs.baseten.co/training/getting-started). The runner snaps the actual training MAX_LENGTH up from dataset stats using finetuning_providers.<backend> policy below. pricing.train_from_usd is a marketing 'from' floor for a typical small LoRA run (Baseten H100 $0.10833/GPU-min = $6.50/h, baseten.co/pricing): ≤14B anchored on Jul 2026 Baseten-invoiced job averages; larger sizes estimated from typical GPU-minutes × rate on 1×H100 (≤72B). pricing.run_from_usd_per_1m_output is serving per 1M output tokens (Modal L4/L40S self-hosted vLLM floors; MoE uses active-param band). group is the marketing library tab label (Group on /models specs); provider comes from providers.display_names. model.marketing holds buyer-facing copy per model (pitch, description, overview, good_for) for the marketing site detail pages. group is only the library tab/filter label. library_filters defines the marketing /models multi-select filters (use_case, tier, context); each model.use_cases lists which use-case filter ids apply. tier/context filters match model.tier and model.context_length against library_filters entries. The order of the models array is the catalog display order within a tier (newest generation first); recommendation ranking is decided by benchmark grades, not by this order.

providers.comment: Friendly display name per model-id prefix (the part before the first '/'), keyed lowercase, under display_names. Used by overbae.services.model_library to label each model's family/provider on the public /library pages. Unknown prefixes fall back to a title-cased version of the raw prefix — add an entry here instead of hardcoding it in Python.

marketing.description: Google DeepMind Gemma 4 open models: hybrid thinking, 140+ languages, dense and MoE sizes from edge to server.
marketing.overview: Gemma 4 26B-A4B is the MoE instruct checkpoint for computer-use style jobs: strong quality with active-param serve cost closer to a mid model. Prefer over 31B when latency and VRAM matter more than peak scores.
good_for: QLoRA when dense 31B is too heavy

marketing.pitch: Large Llama 3.3 instruct for quality-sensitive agents that still want open weights.
marketing.description: Meta's instruct models, all three trainable at their full 128K context. The natural choice when your rows are long and you want a compact model.
marketing.overview: Llama 3 on Overmind covers Meta's instruct models at 1B, 3B, and 8B, each trainable at their full 128K context. Pick this family when your rows are long and you still want a compact model you can serve cheaply after training.

marketing.pitch: Meta's 30B multimodal agentic model — tool use, coding, screenshots.
marketing.description: Muse Glimmer is Meta Superintelligence Lab's open-weight 30B dense multimodal model for local agentic workflows.
marketing.overview: LoRA-only on Overmind. Strong tool-calling and coding agents with vision via a perception encoder; Full FT disabled.
good_for: Long-horizon planning with controllable reasoning strength

marketing.pitch: NVIDIA's 30B/3B-active hybrid MoE for high-volume agent execution.
marketing.description: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a 30B total / 3B active hybrid reasoning MoE for tool calls, validation, and subagent work in long-running agents.
marketing.overview: LoRA-only on Overmind via Unsloth. Native 256K context, Qwen-style tools, thinking off by default. Full FT disabled.
